choices: To hell, to the sides of the pit
explanation: "Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit."

question: What does the LORD say he will cut off from Babylon?
choices: The name, the remnant, son and nephew
explanation: "I will rise up against them... and cut off from Babylon the name, and remnant, and son, and nephew."

question: What will Babylon become a possession for?
choices: The bittern and pools of water
explanation: "I will also make it a possession for the bittern, and pools of water."

question: With what does the LORD say he will sweep Babylon?
explanation: "I will sweep it with the besom of destruction, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: Whom does the LORD say he will break in his land?
explanation: "I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot."

question: What did the LORD found, in the answer to the messengers of the nation?
explanation: "The LORD hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it."

question: Who will be joined with the house of Jacob and cleave to it?
explanation: "The strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob."

question: What will Israel do to those whose captives they were?
choices: Take them captive and rule over them
explanation: "They shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors."

question: From what three things will the LORD give Israel rest?
explanation: "The LORD shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve."

question: Besides the oppressor, what is said to have ceased in the proverb?
explanation: "How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!"

question: What is moved to meet the king at his coming?
explanation: "Hell from beneath is moved for thee to meet thee at thy coming."

question: What do the dead say to the fallen king?
choices: "Art thou also become weak as we?"
explanation: "All they shall speak and say unto thee, Art thou also become weak as we? art thou become like unto us?"

question: What does the king say he will exalt above the stars of God?
explanation: "I will exalt my throne above the stars of God."

question: Where does the king say he will sit?
choices: On the throne of David in Zion
Mount of the congregation, in the north
On the high places of Lebanon
explanation: "I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north."

question: Whom does the king say he will be like?
explanation: "I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the most High."

question: What did the king never do for his prisoners?
explanation: "That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof; that opened not the house of his prisoners?"

question: What did the king make of the world?
explanation: "That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof."

question: To what is the king compared when he is cast out of his grave?
explanation: "Thou art cast out of thy grave like an abominable branch."

question: Why will the king not be joined with the other kings in burial?
choices: He destroyed his land and slew his people
He rose against the LORD of hosts
He took the throne by force
explanation: "Thou shalt not be joined with them in burial, because thou hast destroyed thy land, and slain thy people."

question: For whose iniquity is slaughter to be prepared for the king's children?
explanation: "Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers."

question: What has the LORD of hosts done, saying "as I have purposed, so shall it stand"?
explanation: "The LORD of hosts hath sworn, saying, Surely as I have thought, so shall it come to pass."

question: What will depart from off Israel's shoulders when the Assyrian is broken?
explanation: "Then shall his yoke depart from off them, and his burden depart from off their shoulders."

question: Where does the LORD say he will tread the Assyrian under foot?
explanation: "I will break the Assyrian in my land, and upon my mountains tread him under foot."

question: What will come out of the serpent's root, Palestina is warned?
explanation: "Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina... for out of the serpent's root shall come forth a cockatrice."

question: What will the cockatrice's fruit be?
explanation: "His fruit shall be a fiery flying serpent."

question: Who shall feed, and who shall lie down in safety?
choices: The firstborn of the poor and the needy
The sons of Jacob and the strangers
explanation: "The firstborn of the poor shall feed, and the needy shall lie down in safety."

question: With what will the LORD kill Palestina's root?
explanation: "I will kill thy root with famine, and he shall slay thy remnant."

question: What shall come from the north against Palestina?
explanation: "There shall come from the north a smoke, and none shall be alone in his appointed times."

question: What is broken, so that Palestina should not rejoice?
choices: The rod of him that smote her
explanation: "Rejoice not thou, whole Palestina, because the rod of him that smote thee is broken."

question: What do onlookers ask about the fallen king?
choices: "Is this the man that made the earth to tremble?"
explanation: "Is this the man that made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms?"

question: What is said to be stretched out upon all the nations?
explanation: "This is the purpose that is purposed upon the whole earth: and this is the hand that is stretched out upon all the nations."

question: Whom does hell raise up from their thrones to meet the king?
choices: All the kings of the nations
explanation: "It stirreth up the dead for thee... it hath raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations."

question: The seed of whom shall never be renowned?
explanation: "The seed of evildoers shall never be renowned."

question: What are the gate and the city told to do?
explanation: "Howl, O gate; cry, O city; thou, whole Palestina, art dissolved."

question: Where do all the kings of the nations lie in glory?
choices: Every one in his own house
explanation: "All the kings of the nations, even all of them, lie in glory, every one in his own house."

question: What did the one fallen from heaven weaken?
explanation: "How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!"

question: Which two cities of Moab are laid waste in the night?
explanation: "In the night Ar of Moab is laid waste... in the night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to silence."

question: Where does Moab go up to weep?
choices: Bajith and Dibon, the high places
explanation: "He is gone up to Bajith, and to Dibon, the high places, to weep."

question: What will be on all the heads of Moab, and what of every beard?
choices: Baldness, and every beard cut off
explanation: "On all their heads shall be baldness, and every beard cut off."

question: Where shall the fugitives of Moab flee?
explanation: "His fugitives shall flee unto Zoar, an heifer of three years old."

question: What will the people of Moab carry away to the brook of the willows?
choices: Their harvest of corn and wine
The abundance they have gotten and laid up
explanation: "The abundance they have gotten, and that which they have laid up, shall they carry away to the brook of the willows."

question: Heshbon and Elealeh cry, and their voice is heard even unto where?
explanation: "Heshbon shall cry, and Elealeh: their voice shall be heard even unto Jahaz."

question: To what is Zoar likened?
choices: An heifer of three years old
explanation: "Unto Zoar, an heifer of three years old."

question: What shall the waters of Dimon be full of?
explanation: "The waters of Dimon shall be full of blood: for I will bring more upon Dimon."

question: What does the LORD say he will bring upon those of Moab who escape?
explanation: "I will bring more upon Dimon, lions upon him that escapeth of Moab, and upon the remnant of the land."

question: Who cry out, so that their lives are grievous to them?
explanation: "Therefore the armed soldiers of Moab shall cry out; his life shall be grievous unto him."

question: Whom is Moab told to hide?
explanation: "Hide the outcasts; bewray not him that wandereth."

question: What is Moab told to make as the night in the midst of the noonday?
explanation: "Make thy shadow as the night in the midst of the noonday."

question: What will the one who sits on the throne in the tabernacle of David do?
choices: Judge, seek judgment and haste righteousness
explanation: "He shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging, and seeking judgment, and hasting righteousness."

question: What does the LORD say of Moab's lies?
explanation: "We have heard of the pride of Moab... but his lies shall not be so."

question: Whose foundations shall Moab mourn?
explanation: "For the foundations of Kir-hareseth shall ye mourn; surely they are stricken."

question: Whose vine is said to languish, with the fields of Heshbon?
explanation: "The fields of Heshbon languish, and the vine of Sibmah."

question: What happens when weary Moab comes to his sanctuary to pray?
choices: He shall be heard from heaven
He shall be turned back by Judah
explanation: "Moab is weary on the high place, that he shall come to his sanctuary to pray; but he shall not prevail."

question: Where shall the daughters of Moab be, like a wandering bird?
choices: At the brook of the willows
explanation: "As a wandering bird cast out of the nest, so the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon."

question: What does the LORD say has come to an end in the land?
explanation: "The extortioner is at an end, the spoiler ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land."

question: Within three years, as the years of what?
explanation: "Within three years, as the years of an hireling, the glory of Moab shall be contemned."

question: With whose weeping does the LORD say he will bewail the vine of Sibmah?
explanation: "I will bewail with the weeping of Jazer the vine of Sibmah."

question: What will the treaders tread out no more of in the presses?
explanation: "The treaders shall tread out no wine in their presses; I have made their vintage shouting to cease."

question: To what does the LORD liken the sound of his bowels for Moab?
explanation: "My bowels shall sound like an harp for Moab."

question: What is Moab asked to be to the outcasts?
explanation: "Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler."

question: What is taken away from the plentiful field?
explanation: "Gladness is taken away, and joy out of the plentiful field."

question: What will the remnant of Moab be?
explanation: "The remnant shall be very small and feeble."

question: What will the forsaken cities of Aroer be for?
explanation: "The cities of Aroer are forsaken: they shall be for flocks, which shall lie down, and none shall make them afraid."

question: What will happen to the glory of Jacob in that day?
explanation: "The glory of Jacob shall be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh shall wax lean."

question: Where does the harvestman gather ears of corn?
explanation: "As he that gathereth ears in the valley of Rephaim."

question: What will a man not look to, in that day?
choices: The altars, groves and images made by his hands
explanation: "He shall not look to the altars, the work of his hands... either the groves, or the images."

question: Why will their harvest be a heap in the day of grief?
choices: They forgot the God of their salvation
explanation: "Thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, and hast not been mindful of the rock of thy strength."

question: To what is the rushing of the nations compared?
choices: The noise of the seas and mighty waters
explanation: "Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas."

question: What does God do to the rushing nations?
choices: He gives them over to Assyria
He rebukes them and they flee far off
explanation: "God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off."

question: From where shall the kingdom cease, as the fortress ceases from Ephraim?
explanation: "The fortress also shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria."

question: What does the harvestman gather and reap with his arm?
explanation: "As when the harvestman gathereth the corn, and reapeth the ears with his arm."

question: To what are the fleeing nations compared?
choices: Chaff and a rolling thing before the wind
explanation: "Chased as the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like a rolling thing before the whirlwind."

question: Of what has the forgetful people not been mindful?
explanation: "Hast not been mindful of the rock of thy strength."

question: When does trouble come, and by when is the enemy gone?
choices: Trouble at noon, gone by evening
Trouble at midnight, gone by noon
Trouble at eveningtide, gone before the morning
Trouble at harvest, gone by winter
explanation: "Behold at eveningtide trouble; and before the morning he is not."

question: Whose portion and lot is this, according to the end of the chapter?
choices: Them that spoil and rob us
explanation: "This is the portion of them that spoil us, and the lot of them that rob us."

question: To what will the strong cities be like in that day?
choices: A forsaken bough and an uppermost branch
A city set on a hill
explanation: "His strong cities be as a forsaken bough, and an uppermost branch, which they left."

question: With what shall the forgetful people set their pleasant plants?
explanation: "Therefore shalt thou plant pleasant plants, and shalt set it with strange slips."

question: The remnant of Syria shall be as the glory of whom?
explanation: "The remnant of Syria: they shall be as the glory of the children of Israel, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: What does the LORD lift up on the mountains?
explanation: "See ye, when he lifteth up an ensign on the mountains; and when he bloweth a trumpet, hear ye."

question: What does the LORD say he will do in his dwelling place?
explanation: "I will take my rest, and I will consider in my dwelling place."

question: What does the LORD cut off with pruninghooks before the harvest?
explanation: "He shall both cut off the sprigs with pruninghooks, and take away and cut down the branches."

question: To whom shall the cut-down branches be left?
choices: The fowls of the mountains and the beasts of the earth
explanation: "They shall be left together unto the fowls of the mountains, and to the beasts of the earth."

question: To what place is the present brought unto the LORD of hosts?
explanation: "To the place of the name of the LORD of hosts, the mount Zion."

question: Beyond the rivers of which land does Woe come upon the land shadowing with wings?
explanation: "Woe to the land shadowing with wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia."

question: What will the fowls do upon the cut-down branches?
choices: Feed upon them in the morning
Fly over them in the night
explanation: "The fowls shall summer upon them, and all the beasts of the earth shall winter upon them."

question: What have the rivers done to the scattered nation's land?
explanation: "A nation meted out and trodden down, whose land the rivers have spoiled."

question: What is ripening in the flower before the harvest?
explanation: "Afore the harvest, when the bud is perfect, and the sour grape is ripening in the flower."

question: Besides a clear heat upon herbs, to what is the LORD's consideration likened?
choices: A rain upon the mown grass
A cloud of dew in the heat of harvest
explanation: "I will consider in my dwelling place like a clear heat upon herbs, and like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."

question: Whom does the LORD say he will set against the Egyptians?
explanation: "I will set the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they shall fight every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour."

question: To whom will the LORD give the Egyptians over?
choices: A cruel lord and a fierce king
explanation: "The Egyptians will I give over into the hand of a cruel lord; and a fierce king shall rule over them."

question: Who shall mourn and lament as the waters fail?
explanation: "The fishers also shall mourn, and all they that cast angle into the brooks shall lament."

question: What are the princes of Zoan called?
explanation: "Surely the princes of Zoan are fools, the counsel of the wise counsellors of Pharaoh is become brutish."

question: What has the LORD mingled in the midst of Egypt?
explanation: "The LORD hath mingled a perverse spirit in the midst thereof."

question: What shall be in the midst of the land of Egypt to the LORD?
explanation: "In that day shall there be an altar to the LORD in the midst of the land of Egypt."

question: What will the LORD do to Egypt, so that they return to him?
explanation: "The LORD shall smite Egypt: he shall smite and heal it: and they shall return even to the LORD."

question: Who shall be the third with Egypt and Assyria?
explanation: "In that day shall Israel be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, even a blessing in the midst of the land."

question: What shall be moved at the LORD's presence in Egypt?
explanation: "The idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence, and the heart of Egypt shall melt."

question: What shall wither, be driven away and be no more by the brooks?
choices: The paper reeds and everything sown
explanation: "The paper reeds by the brooks... and every thing sown by the brooks, shall wither, be driven away, and be no more."

question: Who shall be confounded?
choices: Those who work in fine flax and weave networks
explanation: "They that work in fine flax, and they that weave networks, shall be confounded."

question: What are Pharaoh's wise counsellors asked how they can say to him?
choices: "I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings"
"I am the son of the Nile"
"I am the servant of the gods"
explanation: "How say ye unto Pharaoh, I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?"

question: Whose princes are said to be deceived, besides the princes of Zoan?
explanation: "The princes of Zoan are become fools, the princes of Noph are deceived."

question: To what is Egypt compared in how it errs in every work?
choices: A blind man in the way
A drunken man staggering in his vomit
explanation: "They have caused Egypt to err in every work thereof, as a drunken man staggereth in his vomit."

question: What is said of any work Egypt can do?
choices: It shall be done by Assyria
There shall be none for head or tail, branch or rush
It shall be done in secret
It shall be done by the princes of Noph
explanation: "Neither shall there be any work for Egypt, which the head or tail, branch or rush, may do."

question: To what will Egypt be like in that day?
explanation: "In that day shall Egypt be like unto women: and it shall be afraid and fear."

question: What shall the land of Judah be to Egypt?
explanation: "The land of Judah shall be a terror unto Egypt."

question: What language shall five cities in Egypt speak?
explanation: "Five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the LORD of hosts."

question: What shall one of the five cities be called?
explanation: "One shall be called, The city of destruction."

question: What shall be at the border of Egypt to the LORD?
explanation: "There shall be an altar to the LORD in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar at the border thereof to the LORD."

question: What shall the altar and pillar be to the LORD of hosts?
choices: A place of sacrifice for Israel
explanation: "It shall be for a sign and for a witness unto the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt."

question: What will the LORD send when they cry because of the oppressors?
choices: A saviour, and a great one
explanation: "They shall cry unto the LORD because of the oppressors, and he shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them."

question: What shall the Egyptians do when they know the LORD?
choices: Sacrifice, make oblation and vow a vow
explanation: "The Egyptians shall know the LORD in that day, and shall do sacrifice and oblation; yea, they shall vow a vow unto the LORD, and perform it."

question: What shall there be out of Egypt to Assyria?
explanation: "In that day shall there be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria."

question: With whom shall the Egyptians serve?
explanation: "The Egyptians shall serve with the Assyrians."

question: What is Assyria called in the LORD's blessing?
explanation: "Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance."

question: What shall fail in the midst of Egypt?
explanation: "The spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof."

question: What brooks are emptied and dried up?
explanation: "The brooks of defence shall be emptied and dried up: the reeds and flags shall wither."

question: Who shall be broken in their purposes?
choices: All that make sluices and ponds for fish
explanation: "They shall be broken in the purposes thereof, all that make sluices and ponds for fish."

question: Why shall Egypt be afraid?
choices: Because of the armies of Assyria
Because of a plague of darkness
Because of the shaking of the LORD's hand over it
Because of the wrath of Pharaoh
explanation: "It shall be afraid and fear because of the shaking of the hand of the LORD of hosts, which he shaketh over it."

question: What are the wise men challenged to tell Pharaoh?
choices: When the Nile will rise again
What the LORD of hosts hath purposed upon Egypt
Who shall be the next king
Where the idols shall be hidden
explanation: "Where are thy wise men? and let them tell thee now, and let them know what the LORD of hosts hath purposed upon Egypt."

question: How many cities in Egypt shall speak the language of Canaan?
explanation: "In that day shall five cities in the land of Egypt speak the language of Canaan."

question: What does the LORD say he will destroy in the midst of Egypt?
explanation: "The spirit of Egypt shall fail in the midst thereof; and I will destroy the counsel thereof."

question: What is Israel called in the LORD's blessing?
explanation: "Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel mine inheritance."

question: What was Isaiah told to loose from off his loins?
explanation: "Go and loose the sackcloth from off thy loins, and put off thy shoe from thy foot."

question: What was Isaiah told to put off from his foot?
explanation: "Put off thy shoe from thy foot. And he did so, walking naked and barefoot."

question: How does the LORD describe Isaiah?
explanation: "Like as my servant Isaiah hath walked naked and barefoot three years."

question: Who says, "Behold, such is our expectation"?
explanation: "The inhabitant of this isle shall say in that day, Behold, such is our expectation."

question: From whom do they hope to be delivered?
explanation: "Whither we flee for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria."

question: How will the captives be led away by the king of Assyria?
choices: Young and old, naked and barefoot
explanation: "The king of Assyria lead away the Egyptians prisoners, and the Ethiopians captives, young and old, naked and barefoot."

question: What question do the people of the isle ask?
explanation: "Behold, such is our expectation... and how shall we escape?"

question: By whom did the LORD speak at the same time?
explanation: "At the same time spake the LORD by Isaiah the son of Amoz."

question: What is Isaiah's walking naked and barefoot called, upon Egypt and Ethiopia?
explanation: "Isaiah hath walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and wonder upon Egypt and upon Ethiopia."

question: Which city did Tartan fight against and take?
explanation: "Tartan came unto Ashdod... and fought against Ashdod, and took it."

question: Who are told to go up and besiege?
explanation: "Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Media; all the sighing thereof have I made to cease."

question: What does the watchman see coming?
choices: A chariot of men with a couple of horsemen
explanation: "Behold, here cometh a chariot of men, with a couple of horsemen."

question: What happens to the graven images of Babylon's gods?
choices: They are burned in the fire
They are broken unto the ground
explanation: "Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods he hath broken unto the ground."

question: What does the watchman say cometh, and also the night?
explanation: "The watchman said, The morning cometh, and also the night: if ye will enquire, enquire ye: return, come."

question: To what are the prophet's pangs compared?
choices: A sea tossed by the wind
The pangs of a woman that travaileth
explanation: "Pangs have taken hold upon me, as the pangs of a woman that travaileth."

question: What has been turned into fear for the prophet?
explanation: "The night of my pleasure hath he turned into fear unto me."

question: What are the princes told to anoint?
explanation: "Prepare the table, watch in the watchtower, eat, drink: arise, ye princes, and anoint the shield."

question: What is the watchman set to do?
explanation: "Go, set a watchman, let him declare what he seeth."

question: Besides a chariot of asses, what other chariot does the watchman see?
explanation: "He saw a chariot with a couple of horsemen, a chariot of asses, and a chariot of camels."

question: What does the watchman cry from his watchtower?
explanation: "And he cried, A lion: My lord, I stand continually upon the watchtower in the daytime."

question: What does the prophet call those to whom he declares what he has heard?
choices: My threshing, and the corn of my floor
explanation: "O my threshing, and the corn of my floor: that which I have heard of the LORD of hosts... have I declared unto you."

question: Where shall the travelling companies of Dedanim lodge?
choices: In the desert of the sea
explanation: "The burden upon Arabia. In the forest in Arabia shall ye lodge, O ye travelling companies of Dedanim."

question: Who brought water to him that was thirsty?
choices: The inhabitants of the land of Tema
explanation: "The inhabitants of the land of Tema brought water to him that was thirsty."

question: From what did the people flee?
choices: The swords, the bent bow and the grievousness of war
explanation: "They fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, and from the bent bow, and from the grievousness of war."

question: Who will be diminished, according to the end of the chapter?
choices: The residue of the archers, the mighty men of Kedar
explanation: "The residue of the number of archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, shall be diminished."

question: To what is the coming of the burden compared?
explanation: "As whirlwinds in the south pass through; so it cometh from the desert, from a terrible land."

question: How long is the watchman set in his ward?
explanation: "I stand continually upon the watchtower in the daytime, and I am set in my ward whole nights."

question: What does the watchman say to those who would enquire?
choices: Wait, for the vision is for an appointed time
explanation: "If ye will enquire, enquire ye: return, come."

question: What does the LORD say he has made to cease?
explanation: "A grievous vision is declared unto me... all the sighing thereof have I made to cease."

question: Who is said to have spoken the diminishing of Kedar's archers?
explanation: "The residue of the number of archers... shall be diminished: for the LORD God of Israel hath spoken it."

question: How is the prophet affected at the hearing and seeing of the vision?
explanation: "I was bowed down at the hearing of it; I was dismayed at the seeing of it."

question: From whom has the prophet heard what he declares?
choices: The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel
explanation: "That which I have heard of the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, have I declared unto you."

question: What is said of the slain men of the tumultuous city?
choices: They fell in the valley of vision
They are not slain with the sword
They were buried on the housetops
explanation: "Thy slain men are not slain with the sword, nor dead in battle."

question: What has happened to all the rulers?
choices: They were slain at the gate
They fled together and are bound by the archers
explanation: "All thy rulers are fled together, they are bound by the archers."

question: What does the prophet say he will do, and bids none comfort him?
explanation: "Look away from me; I will weep bitterly, labour not to comfort me."

question: What did the people say as they slew oxen and killed sheep?
choices: "Let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die"
explanation: "Behold joy and gladness, slaying oxen, and killing sheep... let us eat and drink; for to morrow we shall die."

question: What does the LORD say of this iniquity?
choices: It shall be forgiven in a year
It shall be laid on Shebna alone
It shall not be purged till they die
It shall be carried to Babylon
explanation: "Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till ye die, saith the Lord GOD of hosts."

question: Whom does the LORD call "my servant" to replace Shebna?
explanation: "I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah."

question: As what will the LORD fasten Eliakim?
choices: A nail in a sure place
explanation: "I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place; and he shall be for a glorious throne to his father's house."

question: Into what will the LORD toss Shebna like a ball?
explanation: "He will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die."

question: What has Shebna hewed out for himself?
explanation: "Thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre here, as he that heweth him out a sepulchre on high."

question: Whose robe and girdle will Eliakim be given?
explanation: "I will clothe him with thy robe, and strengthen him with thy girdle, and I will commit thy government into his hand."

question: What will Eliakim be to the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
explanation: "He shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah."

question: What is said of what Eliakim opens and shuts?
choices: He opens the temple but shuts the city
He opens the gates for the king alone
He shuts the treasures from the poor
He opens and none shuts; he shuts and none opens
explanation: "He shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open."

question: Who bare the quiver with chariots of men and horsemen?
explanation: "And Elam bare the quiver with chariots of men and horsemen, and Kir uncovered the shield."

question: To what did the people look in the house of the forest?
explanation: "Thou didst look in that day to the armour of the house of the forest."

question: What did the people gather together from the lower pool?
explanation: "Ye gathered together the waters of the lower pool."

question: What did the people break down to fortify the wall?
choices: The altars of the high places
explanation: "Ye have numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and the houses have ye broken down to fortify the wall."

question: What did the people make between the two walls?
choices: A ditch for the water of the old pool
explanation: "Ye made also a ditch between the two walls for the water of the old pool."

question: Whom had they not looked unto, though they made the ditch?
explanation: "Ye have not looked unto the maker thereof, neither had respect unto him that fashioned it long ago."

question: What will fill the choicest valleys?
explanation: "Thy choicest valleys shall be full of chariots, and the horsemen shall set themselves in array at the gate."

question: What will the day of trouble do to the walls?
explanation: "A day of trouble, and of treading down... breaking down the walls, and of crying to the mountains."

question: What will happen to the nail fastened in the sure place?
choices: It shall be made of gold
It shall be set on the temple
It shall be removed, cut down and fall
explanation: "The nail that is fastened in the sure place be removed, and be cut down, and fall."

question: What will hang upon Eliakim, the nail?
choices: All the glory of his father's house
explanation: "They shall hang upon him all the glory of his father's house, the offspring and the issue."

question: From what will the LORD drive Shebna?
explanation: "I will drive thee from thy station, and from thy state shall he pull thee down."

question: What will be the shame of his lord's house?
explanation: "There shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory shall be the shame of thy lord's house."

question: What kind of captivity will carry Shebna away?
explanation: "Behold, the LORD will carry thee away with a mighty captivity, and will surely cover thee."

question: Whose son is Eliakim?
explanation: "I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah."

question: How is the city of the valley of vision described?
choices: Full of stirs, tumultuous and joyous
explanation: "Thou that art full of stirs, a tumultuous city, a joyous city."

question: By whom are the fleeing rulers bound?
explanation: "All thy rulers are fled together, they are bound by the archers."

question: The prophet weeps because of the spoiling of whom?
explanation: "I will weep bitterly... because of the spoiling of the daughter of my people."

question: What question does the LORD put to Shebna about his tomb?
choices: "What hast thou here? and whom hast thou here?"
explanation: "What hast thou here? and whom hast thou here, that thou hast hewed thee out a sepulchre here?"

question: Whose city has many breaches that the people have seen?
explanation: "Ye have seen also the breaches of the city of David, that they are many."

question: In what does Shebna grave an habitation for himself?
explanation: "That graveth an habitation for himself in a rock?"

question: What was discovered in that day?
explanation: "He discovered the covering of Judah."

question: What will the LORD commit into Eliakim's hand?
explanation: "I will commit thy government into his hand."

question: Which city is told "Be thou ashamed" because the sea hath spoken?
explanation: The sea spoke to Zidon: "Be thou ashamed, O Zidon: for the sea hath spoken."

question: What is Tyre told to take and carry about the city to be remembered?
explanation: "Take an harp, go about the city, thou harlot that hast been forgotten... that thou mayest be remembered."

question: To what will Tyre's merchandise and hire be given in the end?
explanation: Her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to the LORD.

question: Where is the oppressed daughter of Zidon told she will have no rest?
explanation: "Arise, pass over to Chittim; there also shalt thou have no rest."

question: Why has the LORD of hosts purposed this against Tyre?
choices: To punish her for slaying prophets
To drive her out of the wilderness
To end her trade with Egypt
To stain the pride of all glory
explanation: The LORD of hosts hath purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, and to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth.

question: Whose report is compared to the report of Tyre that brings sore pain?
explanation: As at the report concerning Egypt, so shall they be sorely pained at the report of Tyre.

question: What will Tyre return to after the seventy years, trading with all the kingdoms of the world?
explanation: After the end of seventy years the LORD will visit Tyre, and she shall turn to her hire, and shall commit fornication with all the kingdoms of the world.

question: What did the LORD do against the merchant city after stretching out his hand over the sea?
choices: Shook the kingdoms and commanded its strong holds destroyed
Sent a famine on its fields
explanation: He stretched out his hand over the sea, he shook the kingdoms: the LORD hath given a commandment against the merchant city, to destroy the strong holds thereof.

question: Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of what?
explanation: Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king.

question: Who founded the land of the Chaldeans for them that dwell in the wilderness?
explanation: The Assyrian founded it for them that dwell in the wilderness.

question: What does Tyre's merchandise provide for those who dwell before the LORD?
choices: Silver and gold for the temple
Food to eat sufficiently and durable clothing
explanation: Her merchandise shall be for them that dwell before the LORD, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing.

question: What is Tyre called because the harvest of the river is her revenue?
explanation: By great waters the seed of Sihor, the harvest of the river, is her revenue; and she is a mart of nations.

question: Where are the inhabitants of the isle told to pass over to and howl?
explanation: Pass ye over to Tarshish; howl, ye inhabitants of the isle.

question: What does the sea say it does not do?
explanation: The sea said, "I travail not, nor bring forth children, neither do I nourish up young men."

question: What will be destroyed when the LORD commands judgment against the merchant city?
explanation: The LORD hath given a commandment against the merchant city, to destroy the strong holds thereof.

question: From what land is it revealed to the ships of Tarshish that Tyre is laid waste?
explanation: Howl, ye ships of Tarshish; for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in: from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them.

question: What will not be done with Tyre's merchandise and hire?
choices: It shall not be carried to Zidon
It shall not be sold to Egypt
It shall not be treasured nor laid up
explanation: It shall not be treasured nor laid up.

question: Who is said to have replenished the inhabitants of the isle?
explanation: The merchants of Zidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished the inhabitants of the isle.

question: What became of the towers and palaces raised in the land of the Chaldeans?
choices: They were given to the wilderness folk
explanation: They set up the towers thereof, they raised up the palaces thereof; and he brought it to ruin.

question: Who is told to pass through her land as a river, because there is no more strength?
explanation: Pass through thy land as a river, O daughter of Tarshish: there is no more strength.

question: What does the LORD do to all the honourable of the earth?
explanation: The LORD of hosts hath purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, and to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth.

question: Who is told "Thou shalt no more rejoice" and to arise and pass over to Chittim?
explanation: Thou shalt no more rejoice, O thou oppressed virgin, daughter of Zidon: arise, pass over to Chittim.

question: What does the earth reel to and fro like?
explanation: The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard, and shall be removed like a cottage.

question: Whom does the LORD punish upon the earth, along with the host of the high ones?
explanation: The LORD shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth.

question: What is ashamed when the LORD of hosts reigns in Zion?
explanation: The moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed, when the LORD of hosts shall reign in mount Zion.

question: What has devoured the earth so that the inhabitants are desolate?
explanation: Therefore hath the curse devoured the earth, and they that dwell therein are desolate.

question: Whose name are the people told to glorify in the isles of the sea?
explanation: Glorify ye the LORD in the fires, even the name of the LORD God of Israel in the isles of the sea.

question: Into what does he who flees from the noise of fear fall?
explanation: He who fleeth from the noise of the fear shall fall into the pit.

question: What mourns, while the vine languisheth?
explanation: The new wine mourneth, the vine languisheth, all the merryhearted do sigh.

question: How many men are left after the inhabitants of the earth are burned?
explanation: The inhabitants of the earth are burned, and few men left.

question: What is the broken-down city called?
explanation: The city of confusion is broken down: every house is shut up, that no man may come in.

question: Who languish when the earth mourns and fades away?
choices: The haughty people of the earth
explanation: The earth mourneth and fadeth away, the world languisheth and fadeth away, the haughty people of the earth do languish.

question: The shaking in the midst of the land is likened to what?
choices: The shaking of an olive tree
explanation: There shall be as the shaking of an olive tree, and as the gleaning grapes when the vintage is done.

question: Why does the prophet cry "My leanness, my leanness, woe unto me"?
choices: The treacherous dealers have dealt treacherously
explanation: Isaiah says the treacherous dealers have dealt treacherously, yea, very treacherously.

question: What are open, so that the foundations of the earth shake?
explanation: The windows from on high are open, and the foundations of the earth do shake.

question: How are the high ones and kings gathered together?
explanation: They shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison.

question: What does the LORD do to the inhabitants of the earth in the first verse?
explanation: The LORD maketh the earth empty, and turneth it upside down, and scattereth abroad the inhabitants thereof.

question: What is said of the earth, with its transgression heavy upon it?
choices: It shall fall, and not rise again
It shall be forgiven in time
It shall be washed in the sea
It shall be carried to Zion
explanation: The transgression thereof shall be heavy upon it; and it shall fall, and not rise again.

question: What happens to the prisoners shut up in the prison after many days?
explanation: After many days shall they be visited.

question: What is said to be heard from the uttermost part of the earth?
explanation: From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs, even glory to the righteous.

question: Who is warned that fear, the pit and the snare are upon them?
explanation: Fear, and the pit, and the snare, are upon thee, O inhabitant of the earth.

question: Before whom will the LORD of hosts reign gloriously?
choices: The host of the high ones
explanation: The LORD of hosts shall reign in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, and before his ancients gloriously.

question: What will happen when they drink wine?
choices: They shall not drink it with a song
They shall drink it in the temple
They shall pour it on the ground
They shall sell it to Tyre
explanation: They shall not drink wine with a song; strong drink shall be bitter to them that drink it.

question: What will they do with their voice for the majesty of the LORD, crying from the sea?
explanation: They shall lift up their voice, they shall sing for the majesty of the LORD, they shall cry aloud from the sea.

question: The earth shall be removed like what?
explanation: The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard, and shall be removed like a cottage.

question: Why shall the land be utterly emptied and utterly spoiled?
choices: The LORD hath spoken this word
The people have fled to Tyre
explanation: The land shall be utterly emptied, and utterly spoiled: for the LORD hath spoken this word.

question: He that comes up out of the midst of the pit is taken in what?
explanation: He that cometh up out of the midst of the pit shall be taken in the snare.

question: What shall come of all joy and the mirth of the land?
choices: It is hidden in the sea
All joy is darkened and the mirth gone
explanation: There is a crying for wine in the streets; all joy is darkened, the mirth of the land is gone.

question: What ceases, along with the mirth of tabrets and the noise of them that rejoice?
explanation: The mirth of tabrets ceaseth, the noise of them that rejoice endeth, the joy of the harp ceaseth.

question: Who else does the LORD punish on high, besides the kings of the earth upon the earth?
choices: The host of the high ones
explanation: The LORD shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth.

question: What does the LORD do to the earth, besides making it empty and waste?
explanation: The LORD maketh the earth empty, and maketh it waste, and turneth it upside down.

question: What is left in the city, and what is smitten with destruction?
choices: Silence is left and the wall is broken
Fear is left and the tower falls
Smoke is left and the market burns
Desolation is left and the gate is smitten
explanation: In the city is left desolation, and the gate is smitten with destruction.

question: What shall become of strong drink to those who drink it?
explanation: Strong drink shall be bitter to them that drink it.

question: Who sigh when the new wine mourns and the vine languishes?
explanation: The new wine mourneth, the vine languisheth, all the merryhearted do sigh.

question: What will God wipe away from off all faces?
explanation: The Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces.

question: What has the LORD been to the poor and needy in his distress?
choices: A strength and a refuge from the storm
explanation: Thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat.

question: What will the LORD destroy in this mountain?
choices: The flocks of the terrible ones
The covering cast over all people
explanation: He will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people, and the vail that is spread over all nations.

question: What will the strong people and the terrible nations do after the ruin of the city?
explanation: Therefore shall the strong people glorify thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear thee.

question: What will the people say in that day about their God?
choices: He is a God afar off
We have waited for him, and he will save us
explanation: It shall be said in that day, Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us.

question: What will the LORD take away from off all the earth?
explanation: The rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the LORD hath spoken it.

question: What does the LORD do to the fortress of the high fort of thy walls?
choices: Brings it down to the dust
explanation: The fortress of the high fort of thy walls shall he bring down, lay low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust.

question: Where shall the hand of the LORD rest?
explanation: For in this mountain shall the hand of the LORD rest, and Moab shall be trodden down under him.

question: He shall spread forth his hands in the midst of Moab like whom?
explanation: He shall spread forth his hands in the midst of them, as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim.

question: What will the LORD bring down as the heat in a dry place?
explanation: Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers, as the heat in a dry place.

question: The LORD's counsels of old are what?
explanation: Thy counsels of old are faithfulness and truth.

question: What shall be brought low like heat with the shadow of a cloud?
choices: The branch of the terrible ones
explanation: Even the heat with the shadow of a cloud: the branch of the terrible ones shall be brought low.

question: What is said of the palace of strangers?
choices: It shall be given to Zion
It shall be a house of prayer
explanation: A palace of strangers to be no city; it shall never be built.

question: What does the speaker promise to do to the LORD, his God?
choices: Exalt him and praise his name
explanation: O LORD, thou art my God; I will exalt thee, I will praise thy name.

question: In what land shall the song of the strong city be sung?
explanation: In that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah; We have a strong city.

question: Whose feet tread down the lofty city that the LORD lays low?
choices: The feet of the poor and needy
explanation: The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor, and the steps of the needy.

question: To whom do the people compare themselves in their pain?
choices: A shepherd who lost his flock
A woman with child near her delivery
explanation: Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs; so have we been in thy sight.

question: Where are God's people told to hide until the indignation is overpast?
choices: In their chambers, with the doors shut
explanation: Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment.

question: Who are the people told to trust for ever?
explanation: Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength.

question: What shall the earth disclose and no more cover?
explanation: The earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.

question: In whom is everlasting strength?
explanation: In the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength.

question: Who will learn righteousness when God's judgments are in the earth?
explanation: When thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness.

question: Where will the wicked deal unjustly even when shown favour?
explanation: Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness: in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly.

question: Of what shall the wicked be ashamed?
explanation: They shall see, and be ashamed for their envy at the people; yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them.

question: What do the people confess about other lords?
choices: Other lords besides the LORD have had dominion over them
Other lords have fled from Judah
Other lords have made peace with them
Other lords are kings of Tyre
explanation: O LORD our God, other lords besides thee have had dominion over us.

question: What has the LORD done to the memory of those who are dead and shall not rise?
explanation: Therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.

question: What did the people pour out in trouble when the LORD's chastening was upon them?
explanation: LORD, in trouble have they visited thee, they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them.

question: What did the people bring forth after being with child and in pain?
explanation: We have been with child, we have been in pain, we have as it were brought forth wind.

question: What shall the earth do with the dead when they awake?
explanation: The earth shall cast out the dead.

question: Why does the LORD come out of his place?
choices: To punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity
To feed his people with fat things
To raise up a king in Judah
explanation: The LORD cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity.

question: In what way have the people waited for the LORD?
choices: In the way of his judgments
In the chambers of the king
explanation: Yea, in the way of thy judgments, O LORD, have we waited for thee.

question: What does the nation say about who has wrought all their works?
choices: The LORD hath wrought all our works in us
They wrought them by their own hands
explanation: LORD, thou wilt ordain peace for us: for thou also hast wrought all our works in us.

question: What does the LORD do to them that dwell on high?
explanation: He bringeth down them that dwell on high; the lofty city, he layeth it low.

question: The LORD weighs what for the just?
explanation: The way of the just is uprightness: thou, most upright, dost weigh the path of the just.

question: By whom only will the people make mention of the LORD's name?
explanation: Other lords besides thee have had dominion over us: but by thee only will we make mention of thy name.

question: What is the desire of the soul of those who wait for the LORD?
choices: To his name and the remembrance of him
explanation: The desire of our soul is to thy name, and to the remembrance of thee.

question: When the LORD's hand is lifted up, what do the wicked do?
explanation: LORD, when thy hand is lifted up, they will not see: but they shall see, and be ashamed.

question: What shall devour the wicked?
explanation: The fire of thine enemies shall devour them.

question: What did the LORD do to the nation to the ends of the earth?
choices: Increased it and removed it far
explanation: Thou hast increased the nation, O LORD: thou hadst removed it far unto all the ends of the earth.

question: Whom are told to awake and sing?
choices: Them that dwell in the isles
explanation: Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust.

question: What have the people not wrought in the earth?
explanation: We have not wrought any deliverance in the earth; neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen.

question: What will the wicked not behold, even in the land of uprightness?
explanation: In the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the LORD.

question: What does the LORD say leviathan is, besides the piercing serpent?
explanation: The LORD shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent.

question: Who shall take root, blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit?
explanation: He shall cause them that come of Jacob to take root: Israel shall blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit.

question: What does the LORD use to punish leviathan?
choices: His sore and great and strong sword
explanation: The LORD with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan.

question: The LORD says that fury is not in him; what would he do to briers and thorns?
choices: Go through them and burn them together
Cut them down one by one
explanation: Who would set the briers and thorns against me in battle? I would go through them, I would burn them together.

question: By what is the iniquity of Jacob purged?
choices: The altar stones made as chalkstones beaten in sunder
explanation: By this shall the iniquity of Jacob be purged... when he maketh all the stones of the altar as chalkstones that are beaten in sunder.

question: What shall the calf do in the desolate defenced city?
choices: Feed and lie down and consume the branches
explanation: Yet the defenced city shall be desolate: there shall the calf feed, and there shall he lie down, and consume the branches thereof.

question: Why will he that made them show them no mercy?
choices: It is a people of no understanding
explanation: It is a people of no understanding: therefore he that made them will not have mercy on them.

question: How shall the children of Israel be gathered?
explanation: Ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel.

question: Who shall come when the great trumpet is blown?
choices: Those ready to perish in Assyria and the outcasts in Egypt
explanation: They shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt, and shall worship the LORD in the holy mount at Jerusalem.

question: What shall the women do with the withered boughs?
explanation: The boughs thereof are withered, they shall be broken off: the women come, and set them on fire.

question: What shall not stand up when the altar stones are beaten?
explanation: The groves and images shall not stand up.

question: When does the LORD stay his rough wind?
choices: In the day of the east wind
In the day of the trumpet
explanation: He stayeth his rough wind in the day of the east wind.

question: Where does the LORD beat off from the channel of the river to?
explanation: The LORD shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt.

question: What shall the forsaken habitation be left like?
explanation: The defenced city shall be desolate, and the habitation forsaken, and left like a wilderness.

question: What will the LORD slay that is in the sea?
explanation: And he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.

question: What may one do who takes hold of the strength of the LORD?
explanation: Let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; and he shall make peace with me.

question: Who erred through strong drink, so that they stumble in judgment?
explanation: The priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they err in vision, they stumble in judgment.

question: What are all the tables full of?
explanation: All tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean.

question: Whom does the LORD address as ruling the people in Jerusalem?
explanation: Hear the word of the LORD, ye scornful men, that rule this people which is in Jerusalem.

question: What have the scornful men made their refuge?
explanation: We have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves.

question: What shall happen to their covenant with death?
choices: It shall be written in stone
It shall be given to Egypt
explanation: Your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell shall not stand.

question: Who instructs the farmer to discretion?
explanation: For his God doth instruct him to discretion, and doth teach him.

question: What will he that believeth on the sure foundation not do?
explanation: Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste.

question: What will happen to the crown of pride, the drunkards of Ephraim?
choices: They shall be trodden under feet
They shall be crowned with glory
They shall be carried to Zion
They shall be given to Assyria
explanation: The crown of pride, the drunkards of Ephraim, shall be trodden under feet.

question: What will the LORD of hosts be for the residue of his people?
choices: A crown of glory and a diadem of beauty
explanation: In that day shall the LORD of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people.

question: What does the LORD have, which is as a tempest of hail and a destroying storm?
explanation: Behold, the Lord hath a mighty and strong one, which as a tempest of hail and a destroying storm shall cast down to the earth.

question: What befalls those to whom the word is precept upon precept?
choices: They go and fall backward, and are broken and snared
They are made wise and rich
explanation: The word of the LORD was unto them precept upon precept, that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.

question: The glorious beauty of the fat valley is likened to what?
choices: The hasty fruit before the summer
explanation: The glorious beauty shall be a fading flower, and as the hasty fruit before the summer; while it is yet in his hand he eateth it up.

question: The LORD of hosts will be strength to whom?
choices: Them that turn the battle to the gate
explanation: He shall be for strength to them that turn the battle to the gate.

question: Whom shall the LORD teach knowledge, as the scornful ask?
explanation: Whom shall he teach knowledge? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.

question: With what lips will the LORD speak to this people?
explanation: With stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people.

question: What did the people say when told of the rest and refreshing for the weary?
explanation: This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear.

question: What will the LORD lay to the line, and what to the plummet?
choices: Judgment to the line, righteousness to the plummet
Mercy to the line, wrath to the plummet
Peace to the line, strength to the plummet
Wisdom to the line, truth to the plummet
explanation: Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet.

question: What shall sweep away the refuge of lies?
explanation: The hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters shall overflow the hiding place.

question: What is said of the bed and the covering?
choices: The bed is soft and the covering warm
The bed is too short and the covering too narrow
The bed is empty and the covering torn
The bed is in Zion and the covering in Egypt
explanation: The bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it.

question: In which mount does the LORD say he will rise up?
explanation: The LORD shall rise up as in mount Perazim, he shall be wroth as in the valley of Gibeon.

question: Why are the scornful told not to be mockers?
choices: Lest their bands be made strong
explanation: Now therefore be ye not mockers, lest your bands be made strong.

question: What has the LORD of hosts determined upon the whole earth?
explanation: I have heard from the Lord GOD of hosts a consumption, even determined upon the whole earth.

question: Where does the LORD say he lays the tried stone, the precious corner stone?
